June 15, 2026
Neighborhood Health Center (NHC) is a federally qualified health center (FQHC) headquartered in Washington County, Oregon, committed to our mission to build healthy communities—one neighbor at a time—through patient-centered healthcare, regardless of income or current state of wellness. Neighborhood Health Center (NHC) serves historically underserved communities, including low-income households, communities of color, agricultural workers, as well as individuals experiencing homelessness. In 2025, these sites provided primary medical, dental, behavioral health, and pharmacy services to nearly 25,000 patients through 74,000 visits, many of whom face financial, transportation, and other barriers to care.
analysis:
## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** Neighborhood Health Center (NHC); signed by Jeri Weeks, Chief Executive Officer
- **Stakeholder type:** Healthcare Provider (Federally Qualified Health Center)
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** FQHC headquartered in Washington County, Oregon; nine clinics and two school-based health centers (SBHCs); 26,000+ employees; served 25,000 patients through 74,000 visits in 2025; serves low-income, communities of color, agricultural workers, and individuals experiencing homelessness; pharmacy contact Michele Taney, PharmD

---

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

NHC strongly supports the proposed rule's electronic prior authorization and interoperability goals, viewing them as critical for the medically underserved populations CHCs serve. However, the organization raises extensive safety-net-specific concerns including: vendor readiness gaps, 340B pharmacy workflow complexity, medical/pharmacy benefit classification ambiguity, cybersecurity resource constraints, HTI-5 rule conflicts creating a compliance timing gap, and the need for dedicated federal support and technical assistance for FQHCs. NHC opposes removing drug formulary information from Provider Access/Payer-to-Payer APIs and urges automatic approval for missed PA deadlines.

---

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** FHIR-IG-REQUIRED, PA-DRUG-PHARMACY, PA-DRUG-MEDICAL, PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS, PA-DENIAL-REASONS, API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING, API-USAGE-METRICS, HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS, ONC-STANDARDS-UPDATE, GENERAL
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** CMS-0062-P; HTI-4 (90 FR 37130, Aug 4, 2025); HTI-5 proposed rule; 45 CFR 170.315(g)(31)-(g)(33); CMS-0053-F (claims attachments, compliance May 2028); CMS February 28, 2024 National Standards Group enforcement discretion letter
- **Standards referenced:** FHIR (CRD/DTR/PAS Da Vinci IGs v2.2); X12 278; X12 6020; NCPDP; CDex (Clinical Data Exchange IG); US Core; HL7 Da Vinci Project IGs; ONC certification criteria 45 CFR 170.315(g)(31)-(g)(33)

---

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: API Interoperability — Vendor Readiness and Payer Standardization**
- **Provision ID:** FHIR-IG-REQUIRED
- **Position:** Support with modification
- **Rationale:** CHCs rely on limited EHR vendors and third-party tech partners; absent vendor readiness requirements, CHCs may face compliance gaps despite acting in good faith; inconsistent payer API rollouts will undermine efficiency goals.
- **Specific request:** Clarify providers won't be penalized for vendor/clearinghouse/EHR failures; coordinate CMS implementation timelines with ONC certification requirements; require uniform minimum implementation standards across MCOs and QHP issuers including standardized PA data fields and synchronized IG timelines.

**Topic 2: Cybersecurity and IT Resource Concerns**
- **Provision ID:** FHIR-IG-REQUIRED / API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING
- **Position:** Support with modification
- **Rationale:** Expansion of interoperable exchange increases cybersecurity exposure; CHCs lack dedicated cybersecurity teams and rely on third-party vendors for HIPAA compliance; unfunded costs of cybersecurity compliance, vendor upgrades, and API integration would harm safety-net providers.
- **Specific request:** CMS should provide technical assistance, cybersecurity/IT workforce development support, and dedicated health IT funding for CHCs.

**Topic 3: Electronic PA for Drugs — Medical/Pharmacy Benefit Classification**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL / PA-DRUG-PHARMACY / MEDICAL-VS-PHARMACY-BENEFIT
- **Position:** Support with modification
- **Rationale:** CHCs face a burden managing dual workflows; determining whether a medication falls under medical or pharmacy benefit is not always clear in real time (e.g., extended-release buprenorphine billed under pharmacy benefit when dispensed but medical benefit when administered in-clinic).
- **Specific request:** Require payers to expose benefit classification information through Provider Access APIs (via CRD Coverage Information extension) so providers can determine in real time whether a drug falls under medical or pharmacy benefit; clarify whether PA approval under one benefit pathway also applies to the alternate pathway.

**Topic 4: 340B Pharmacy Workflow Complexity**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-PHARMACY
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Over 65% of CHCs use 340B contract pharmacy arrangements; ePA implementation requires coordination across EHR, pharmacy management systems, contract pharmacies, TPAs, and payer APIs — systems not always interoperable; PA determinations, dispensing data, eligibility, and clinical documentation across separate systems create risk of errors in complex 340B workflows.
- **Specific request:** CMS should coordinate with the Office of Pharmacy Affairs (OPA) to provide targeted technical assistance, implementation guidance, and funding support for CHC 340B pharmacy workflows.

**Topic 5: Proactive PA Expiration Notifications**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL / PA-DRUG-PHARMACY
- **Position:** Modify (additional requirement)
- **Rationale:** Evidence shows proactive outreach before PA expiration achieves positive outcomes in 87% of cases vs. 25% without notification; prevents treatment interruptions and retroactive reauthorization burden.
- **Specific request:** CMS should mandate proactive PA expiration notifications to providers via FHIR-based alerts.

**Topic 6: ePA Without Concurrent PA Reform**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL / PA-DRUG-PHARMACY
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** Peer-reviewed evidence shows providers using ePA submitted higher PA volumes, spent more total time on PA, had greater difficulty identifying step therapy requirements, and experienced slightly decreased medication filling rates compared to non-ePA providers; ePA alone may accelerate an inefficient process.
- **Specific request:** Pair ePA technology mandates with meaningful PA reduction requirements, including Gold Carding for prescription drugs and sunset provisions for PA categories with consistently high approval rates.

**Topic 7: PA Decision Timeframes**
- **Provision ID:** PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Delays disproportionately affect medically underserved CHC patients who cannot afford treatment interruptions; 24-hour standard and 72-hour QHP standard represent meaningful improvement.
- **Specific request:** Add automatic approval for PA requests not decided within required timeframes to ensure compliance.

**Topic 8: Denial Reason Specificity and Public Reporting**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DENIAL-REASONS / API-USAGE-METRICS
- **Position:** Support with expansion
- **Rationale:** Specific denial reasons allow CHCs to efficiently correct submissions and pursue appeals without back-and-forth; public reporting will improve payer accountability.
- **Specific request:** Publish required PA metrics in a centralized, standardized, publicly accessible format on CMS website; expand reporting to include: denial rates by service type/medication category, first-pass approval rates, denials overturned due to inadequate denial notices, and data completeness metrics.

**Topic 9: API Endpoint Reporting**
- **Provision ID:** API-ENDPOINT-REPORTING
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Centralized CMS publication eliminates need for providers to look up each payer's endpoints individually; particularly beneficial for CHCs with small IT departments; hard-coded endpoints cause EHR disruptions when outdated.
- **Specific request:** Publish API endpoint information as machine-readable files; prioritize ease of access for primary care providers in safety net settings, especially rural.

**Topic 10: API Usage Metrics**
- **Provision ID:** API-USAGE-METRICS
- **Position:** Support with expansion
- **Rationale:** Disaggregated Medicaid data by program and plan will reveal access gaps; requires additional metrics to evaluate meaningful API value.
- **Specific request:** Add metrics on: successful API request rates, rejected requests (authorization failures, malformed queries), structured vs. unstructured data in responses, workflow impact, calls per query, queries per user, and cost of maintaining each API.

**Topic 11: Drug Formulary Information Removal**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL (Provider Access/Payer-to-Payer API)
- **Position:** Oppose
- **Rationale:** Formulary lists change rapidly due to PBM exclusions; payer website access is neither reliable nor real-time; CHC providers serving multiple payers cannot conduct manual lookups; providers may delay prescribing or default to suboptimal options without point-of-care formulary access.
- **Specific request:** CMS should reconsider removing drug formulary information from Provider Access and Payer-to-Payer APIs.

**Topic 12: HIPAA PA Standards — X12 to FHIR Transition**
- **Provision ID:** HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS
- **Position:** Support with modification
- **Rationale:** CHCs will need to support both X12 6020 (compliance May 2028) and FHIR/CDex (compliance 2029) simultaneously; limited IT staff makes dual-standard period especially burdensome.
- **Specific request:** Extend February 28, 2024 National Standards Group enforcement discretion (FHIR PA API as X12 278 substitute) to cover the CMS-0062-P transition period.

**Topic 13: CDex Guardrails**
- **Provision ID:** HIPAA-PA-STANDARDS / FHIR-IG-REQUIRED
- **Position:** Support with modification
- **Rationale:** CDex creates mechanism for payers to issue iterative, escalating data requests, increasing provider burden.
- **Specific request:** (1) Require payers to specify all needed documentation in initial CDex request; (2) limit payer solicited-attachment requests to maximum two per PA transaction before issuing decision; (3) establish maximum payer response timeframes after receiving CDex attachments.

**Topic 14: Gold Carding**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL (step therapy RFI)
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** CMS has already implemented gold carding for DMEPOS (90% threshold with WISeR model); CHCs with demonstrated PA compliance should receive exemptions; gold carding would reduce staff time and costs for CHCs operating on thin margins.
- **Specific request:** CMS should publish formal guidance recommending payers implement gold carding; ensure gold carding extends to all items and services for eligible providers, not just specific service categories.

**Topic 15: ONC/HTI-5 Harmonization**
- **Provision ID:** ONC-STANDARDS-UPDATE
- **Position:** Modify
- **Rationale:** HTI-5's proposed removal of 34 of 60 ONC certification criteria may affect supporting infrastructure for ePA workflows; EHR certification deadlines under HTI-4 (December 2027/January 2028) extend beyond CMS-0062-P payer compliance date (October 1, 2027), creating up to 3-month gap when payer APIs are operational but certified provider-facing EHRs are not yet available.
- **Specific request:** CMS and ONC should issue joint implementation guidance ensuring HTI-5 final regulations don't undercut CMS-0062-P; publish formal CMS-ONC harmonization assessment before CMS-0062-P final rule.

---

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

- **S1 (require vs recommend IGs):** Supports requiring FHIR IGs including CRD/DTR/PAS v2.2; notes concern about HTI-5 potentially removing supporting certification criteria.
- **S12 (technical challenges for medical benefit drugs):** Raises 340B pharmacy interoperability, medical/pharmacy benefit classification ambiguity, and EHR/PMS data exchange gaps as significant technical challenges.
- **S15 (medical vs pharmacy distinction):** Requests CMS expose benefit classification through Provider Access API (CRD Coverage Information extension); seeks clarification on dual-pathway coverage situations.
- **S16 (what is specific reason for denial):** Supports requiring specific denial reasons; wants centralized standardized public reporting of denial data.
- **S17 (structured denial codes):** Supports; recommends expanding public metrics to include first-pass approval rates and denials overturned due to inadequate notices.
- **S20 (24-hour achievable):** Supports proposed 24-hour timeframe; urges automatic approval for missed deadlines.
- **S23 (API endpoint security concerns):** Raises cybersecurity concerns for CHCs lacking dedicated security teams; requests CMS provide cybersecurity support and technical assistance.
- **S24 (what to report for endpoints):** Supports proposed endpoint reporting requirements; requests machine-readable format.
- **S26 (format for endpoint reporting):** Supports; recommends machine-readable files for maximum utility.
- **S27 (reporting frequency):** Supports proposed 1-week update requirement and annual verification.
- **S29 (which API usage metrics):** Supports; recommends adding successful/failed request rates, structured vs. unstructured data ratios, and API cost metrics.
- **S30 (privacy protections in metrics):** Not directly addressed.
- **S34 (reporting frequency):** Supports aligning deadlines with reporting periods.
- **S35 (publish aggregate metrics):** Supports CMS publishing trends; encourages centralized standardized publication on CMS website.
- **S44 (FHIR appropriate as HIPAA standard):** Supports FHIR direction; requests enforcement discretion extension during X12-to-FHIR transition.
- **S46 (X12 coexistence):** Notes dual-standard burden during transition (X12 6020 + FHIR/CDex simultaneously); requests enforcement discretion extension.
- **S47 (timeline for HIPAA FHIR standard):** Concerned about timing gap between payer compliance (Oct 2027) and EHR certification availability (Dec 2027-Jan 2028).
- **S50 (IG maturity):** Notes CDex creates iterative data request mechanism; recommends guardrails.
- **S60 (ONC versioning approach):** Supports CMS-ONC harmonization; concerned HTI-5 may inadvertently remove supporting infrastructure for ePA.
- **S61 (CMS-ONC coordination):** Explicitly requests joint CMS-ONC guidance and formal harmonization assessment before final rule.
- **S62 (testing criteria):** Requests CMS clarify providers won't be penalized for vendor failures; recommends readiness validation before enforcement.
- **S65 (industry adoption rates):** Notes EHR certification timing gap; urges CMS ensure providers not held non-compliant for unavailable certified technology.
- **Step therapy RFI:** Supports gold carding for prescription drugs; references existing WISeR model and DMEPOS precedent; recommends formal payer guidance and service-agnostic application.
- **Lab/DMEPOS RFI:** Supports ePA extension but notes technology and interoperability readiness must accompany any expansion.

---

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Clarify that providers will not be penalized for compliance failures attributable to vendors, clearinghouses, or EHR systems outside provider control.
2. Coordinate implementation timelines with ONC certification requirements; establish readiness validation before enforcement begins.
3. Require uniform minimum implementation standards across MCOs and QHP issuers (standardized PA data fields, synchronized IG timelines).
4. Provide technical assistance, cybersecurity/IT workforce development support, and dedicated health IT funding for CHCs.
5. Require payers to expose benefit classification via Provider Access API (CRD Coverage Information extension) so providers can determine medical vs. pharmacy benefit in real time.
6. Clarify whether PA approval under one benefit pathway applies to the alternate pathway for dual-pathway drugs.
7. Coordinate with Office of Pharmacy Affairs to provide technical assistance and funding for CHC 340B pharmacy workflow integration.
8. Mandate proactive PA expiration notifications to providers via FHIR-based alerts.
9. Pair ePA mandates with PA reduction requirements including Gold Carding and sunset provisions for high-approval-rate PA categories.
10. Require automatic approval for PA requests not decided within required timeframes.
11. Publish required PA metrics in centralized, standardized, publicly accessible CMS website format.
12. Expand reporting metrics to include: denial rates by service type/medication category, first-pass approval rates, denials overturned due to inadequate denial notices, and data completeness metrics.
13. Publish API endpoint information as machine-readable files; prioritize ease of access for safety-net/rural providers.
14. Add API usage metrics: successful/failed request rates, structured vs. unstructured data ratios, workflow impact, and API maintenance costs.
15. Reconsider removing drug formulary information from Provider Access and Payer-to-Payer APIs.
16. Extend February 28, 2024 enforcement discretion to cover the CMS-0062-P transition period from X12 to FHIR.
17. Require payers to specify all documentation in initial CDex requests; limit to two solicited-attachment requests per PA transaction before issuing decision; establish maximum payer response timeframes after receiving CDex attachments.
18. Issue formal guidance recommending payers implement gold carding for all items and services (not just specific categories) for eligible providers.
19. Publish joint CMS-ONC implementation guidance ensuring HTI-5 does not undercut CMS-0062-P; complete formal harmonization assessment before final rule.
20. Ensure safety-net providers are prioritized for federal matching funds to cover implementation costs.

---

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:** Vendor readiness gaps leaving CHCs unable to comply despite good faith; cybersecurity exposure with insufficient resources; medical/pharmacy benefit classification ambiguity creating dual-workflow burden; 340B pharmacy system interoperability gaps; dual-standard transition period (X12 + FHIR simultaneously); HTI-5 certification criteria removal potentially removing supporting infrastructure; 3-month timing gap between payer API compliance and certified EHR availability.
- **Potential negative impacts cited:** CHC compliance gaps from vendor failures; unfunded cybersecurity costs; treatment interruptions for medically underserved patients from ePA without concurrent PA reform; 340B workflow errors; disruption for 65%+ of CHCs using contract pharmacies.
- **Implementation barriers mentioned:** Limited CHC IT staff and budgets; EHR/PMS interoperability gaps; lack of dedicated cybersecurity teams; complex 340B workflows across multiple systems; HTI-5 certification timing gap; nearly half of CHCs with fewer than 90 days cash on hand; average operating margins now negative for CHC sector.

---

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:** 94% of physicians report PA delays patient care (AMA survey); average PA wait time ~3 days with one-third waiting >1 week; 53 million MA PA determinations in 2024 including 4+ million full/partial denials (KFF); 90%+ of CHC patients below 200% FPL; 65%+ of CHCs use 340B contract pharmacy; proactive PA expiration outreach achieves 87% positive outcomes vs. 25% without; ePA associated with higher PA volumes and slightly decreased medication fill rates (Lauffenburger et al., 2021).
- **Studies or research referenced:** AMA prior authorization survey; KFF MA PA determinations 2024; MGMA prior authorization landscape report 2025; NACHC 2025 NTTAP HIT Needs Assessment; Lauffenburger JC et al. J Am Med Inform Assoc. 2021; Salzbrenner SG et al. J Manag Care Spec Pharm. 2022; Vishwanath S et al. Am J Manag Care. 2021; Krauss ZJ et al. Pharmacy (Basel). 2022; 2024 HRSA UDS data.
- **Examples provided:** Extended-release buprenorphine billed under pharmacy benefit when dispensed but medical benefit when administered in-clinic; specific clinic-by-clinic patient data for NHC's Washington/Clackamas county sites.

---

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:** FQHCs/CHCs; medically underserved patients (low-income, homeless, agricultural workers, communities of color); 340B program participants; CHC IT/pharmacy staff; EHR and PMS vendors serving safety-net markets.
- **Economic implications:** CHC sector operating margins negative; half of CHCs with fewer than 90 days cash; unfunded vendor upgrade, API integration, and cybersecurity costs would be severely burdensome; gold carding and automatic approval would reduce administrative costs.
- **Technical feasibility:** Notes significant technical barriers specific to safety-net settings: limited IT staff, EHR/PMS interoperability gaps, 340B system complexity, lack of cybersecurity teams. HTI-5 timing gap creates 3-month window where payer APIs operational but certified EHRs unavailable.
- **Patient care impact:** Delays disproportionately harm CHC patients facing non-clinical health factors; 340B medication access depends on smooth PA workflows; loss of formulary information from APIs will harm prescribing decisions for providers without administrative infrastructure for manual lookups.

---

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Mixed (strongly supportive of goals with extensive safety-net-specific modification requests)
- **Tone:** Professional, Collaborative, Detailed
- **Priority level:** High

---

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "CMS should clarify that providers will not be penalized for failures attributable to vendors, clearinghouses, or EHR systems outside provider control." - Context: Discussing vendor readiness gaps that could create compliance failures for CHCs acting in good faith.

2. "ePA without concurrent PA reform may merely accelerate an inefficient process." - Context: Citing peer-reviewed evidence that ePA implementation alone increased PA volumes and didn't improve medication fill rates; urging paired PA reduction requirements.

3. "CHCs and their clearinghouses will need to support both standards simultaneously during transition: X12 6020 for claims attachments (CMS-0053-F, compliance May 2028) and FHIR/CDex for PA attachments (CMS-0062-P, compliance in 2029). This dual-standard burden is real and must be acknowledged." - Context: Requesting extension of enforcement discretion during X12-to-FHIR transition.

4. "CHCs and other providers cannot be considered non-compliant for failing to use technology that does not yet exist in certified form." - Context: Highlighting the 3-month gap between payer API compliance (Oct 2027) and certified EHR availability (Dec 2027-Jan 2028) under HTI-4 timelines.

---

## 12. THEMES

- [x] **IMPLEMENTATION-TIMELINE** - Raises HTI-4/HTI-5 certification timing gap relative to Oct 2027 payer compliance; dual-standard transition period burden; requests enforcement discretion extension.
- [x] **COST-RESOURCES** - Extensively documents CHC financial constraints: negative sector margins, <90 days cash, unfunded cybersecurity/vendor upgrade costs, unreimbursed PA staff time.
- [x] **PROVIDER-BURDEN** - Central focus: manual PA processes, payer variability, CDex iterative data requests, and 340B workflow complexity all increase CHC provider burden.
- [x] **PRIVACY-SECURITY** - Raises cybersecurity exposure concerns specific to CHCs lacking dedicated IT security teams and relying on third-party vendors.
- [x] **HEALTH-EQUITY** - Extensive: CHC patient demographics (40% Hispanic/Latinx, homeless, agricultural workers, rural communities); delays disproportionately harm those unable to afford treatment interruptions.
- [x] **TECHNICAL-FEASIBILITY** - Multiple technical barriers: EHR/PMS interoperability gaps, 340B system complexity, HTI-5 certification criteria removal, lack of FHIR integration in pharmacy systems.
- [x] **STANDARDS-MATURITY** - CDex guardrails needed; HTI-5 conflicts with CMS-0062-P IG requirements; requests CMS-ONC harmonization assessment.
- [x] **PATIENT-ACCESS** - Core motivation: PA delays harm underserved CHC patients; automatic approval and proactive expiration alerts would protect medication access.
- [ ] **REGULATORY-AUTHORITY** - Not addressed.
- [x] **STAKEHOLDER-COORDINATION** - Urges CMS-ONC coordination; CMS-OPA coordination for 340B; vendor accountability requirements; safety-net provider implementation support.
- [x] **MEDICAL-VS-PHARMACY-BENEFIT** - Explicitly raises benefit classification ambiguity for CHCs; requests Provider Access API exposure of benefit classification via CRD Coverage Information extension.
- [x] **TRANSPARENCY** - Supports specific denial reasons; requests centralized CMS publication of PA metrics; opposes formulary data removal from APIs.
- [x] **SMALL-PAYER-IMPACT** - Directly applicable to safety-net providers: limited resources, thin margins, small IT departments, resource constraints comparable to small payers.
- [x] **EXISTING-WORKFLOWS** - 340B pharmacy workflow integration; dual-standard transition; ePA without PA reform may increase total PA burden.
- [x] **VENDOR-ECOSYSTEM** - Extensive: CHC dependence on limited EHR vendors; HTI-5 vendor deprioritization risk; EHR/PMS interoperability gaps; need for vendor accountability requirements.
